java_locations.role: Legacy font-family resolution checks each requested FontParam-specific `<param>fontname` key, then `defaultfontname`; it never reads a generic `fontname` key.
Constructs the accepted specific keys from the FontParam enum name and the `fontname` suffix.
Separately maps the legitimate `defaultFontName` legacy key to the root style `fontName` property.

rust_locations.role: Raw legacy skinparam resolvers and capability predicates currently admit `fontName` alongside specific state/arrow keys and `defaultFontName`.
Resolved style `fontName` properties are legitimate style-cascade inputs and are not part of the defect.

claimed_invariant: Every state font-family consumer follows the same Java legacy precedence: a matching FontParam-specific key, then `defaultFontName`, then the FontParam default. A raw generic `fontName` skinparam has no effect. A resolved CSS/style `fontName` property remains effective.
causal_divergence: Rust independently accumulated `fontName` as a raw fallback in node, history, transition, autonomous, oracle-assisted, and capability-gate code. Java never consults that key in legacy font lookup. This makes Rust apply Courier or another family to state text and labels that Java leaves at sans-serif, changing intrinsic measurements, Graphviz label boxes, routes, painted bounds, and final SVG dimensions.
planned_model_change: Remove raw `fontName` from every state legacy skinparam resolver and from the autonomous/flat capability allowlists. Preserve specific `stateFontName`, `stateAttributeFontName`, `stateArrowFontName`, `arrowFontName`, and `defaultFontName` precedence. Preserve resolved style-cascade `fontName` handling. Add tests covering ignored raw generic fontName and accepted default/specific/style inputs.
perturbation_axes: state-node text versus transition labels versus history labels
generic fontName versus defaultFontName versus state-specific font names
flat versus nested autonomous state topology
acceptance: The known generic-fontName counterexample is structurally equivalent in the no-oracle comparator.
Fresh held-out inputs show raw generic fontName is inert while defaultFontName and state-specific keys still affect the intended channels.
The full rustuml-render library suite passes.
An independent checker records a verdict at the exact implementation revision.
